messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: increment_log_prob
parts:
Hi all

With the new stan, my model gives a warning, that i havent been able to figure out how to fix, the warning is:

Warning (non-fatal):     sampling statement (~) contains a transformed parameter or local variable.
     You must increment lp__ with the log absolute determinant of the Jacobian of the transform.
     Sampling Statement left-hand-side expression:
          get_base1(mu,i,"mu",1) ~ multi_normal_log(...)

Here is the loop that includes the local variable:

What would be the proper way to implement the increment_log_prob function ?

{
vector[nvars] mu[n]; ///////////

for (i in 1:n){
for (k in 1:nvars){
mu[i,k] <- b[k,id[i],1] + b[k,id[i],2] * x[i];
if (x[i] > b[k,id[i],4])
mu[i,k] <- mu[i,k] + (b[k,id[i],3] * (x[i] - b[k,id[i],4]));
}

y[i] ~ multi_normal(mu[i], Sigma_y);

mu[i] ~ multi_normal(mm, cov_vm);
}
}


Thank you

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] increment_log_prob
parts:
Your model's fine how it is. The warning message is a
false positive in this case. I was meaning to fix it before
the release, but it never made it into an issue that we were
tracking.

You only need to worry about a Jacobian adjustment if you
have a non-linear change of variables. What you have with an
array index isn't even a linear change of variables, it's just
indexing.

We'll fix this for the next release.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] increment_log_prob
parts:
Hi,

I regret that this may be a naive question, but I'm also receiving this warning and unsure of its implications -

I'm building a model that uses the hierarchical re-parameterization described in S19.1 of the reference manual.  In other words, I have "raw" parameters that have a N(0,1) prior and then I have transformed parameters transformed by the scale and width of the hyperprior distribution.

Does this mean I need to add additional code to the model to calculate the Jacobian and increment the logprob in order to accurately sample from the posterior?  If so, is there an example of this in the documentation or sample models?

Thanks for any advice!

~Nathan

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] increment_log_prob
parts:
The transformation chapter of the manual explains when
you need a Jacobian adjustment and when you don't.

The short answer is that you only need a Jacobian adjustment
if you use a transformed variable on the left-hand side of
a sampling statement. The reparameterization you're talking
about won't need one, because it's the raw (untransformed)
parameters that show up with the normal(0,1).

- Bob
